t: A dynasty from western India that ruled northern India from Kannauj between the early 9th and early 10th centuries.
Its cavalry checked Arab expansion beyond Sindh and Multan, and Arab writers thought its king the most hostile to them in India.
It fought the Palas and Rashtrakutas for Kannauj, and its feudatories became the later Rajput kingdoms.
dyk: An inscription of 876 at the Chaturbhuj temple in Gwalior Fort, set up under Mihira Bhoja, contains one of the earliest known inscribed zeros in India.
ev: Nagabhata I repels Arab armies advancing from Sindh
The Rashtrakuta Dhruva defeats Vatsaraja and drives him from the Doab
Nagabhata II takes Kannauj from the Ayudha dynasty and makes it the capital
Mihira Bhoja begins a reign of almost fifty years
An Arab merchant praises the cavalry and security of the Gurjara kingdom
The Rashtrakuta Indra III sacks Kannauj
Mahmud of Ghazni takes Kannauj after Rajyapala abandons it
Last inscription of the dynasty, issued by Yashahpala

f.capital: Ujjain or Jalor (uncertain); Kannauj from c. 816
f.successor: Gahadavala dynasty; Chandela and Paramara dynasties
